plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.

conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and concentrating on income and quality names, with a larger cash buffer.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%) to a small allocation.
Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration.
Add QQQI to 10% for income.
Buy MSFT at 10% as a quality tech addition.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
It aims for steady growth with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly returns by focusing on risk reduction first. It lowers leverage and concentration while adding quality names and income, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 6%, SPAL to 6%) for amplified returns.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration.
Buy MSFT at 10% as a core tech holding.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly returns by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-conviction tech names, accepting higher potential drawdowns and the risk of amplified losses due to leverage and daily rebalancing of ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Maximize QQQI to 30% for steady income.
Trim SPY to 20% to free up capital for income.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly returns through distributions. It shifts heavily into income-generating assets like QQQI, cuts all leverage and high-beta names, and maintains a cash buffer. While prioritizing income, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
